Paint wall to wall and clean up
New compound absorbs paint differently, so spot-painting flashes. We prime and paint corner to corner, contain the dust, and leave the room clean.

Real Leander numbers: minimum service call $200-$350, small hole (doorknob or fist-sized) $200-$400, medium hole up to about 12 inches $300-$550, single crack $250-$450, water-damaged ceiling section $600-$1,500, full sheet $250-$500. You are not paying for the patch material, which costs almost nothing. You are paying for 2 to 4 trips, overnight drying between coats, texture matching and paint. Pro tip: batch repairs. Five patches in one visit costs far less than five separate calls, so walk the house and make a list first.
When should I NOT hire you and do it myself instead?

Do it yourself: filling small nail holes before painting, a hairline crack in a wall you are already repainting, or a small hole in a garage, closet or utility room where looks do not matter. Do not do it yourself: anything on a textured wall you care about, anything on a ceiling, anything in a bright formal room where side light shows every flaw, and anything wet. The most common job we do is the second attempt, fixing a self-repair that is now bigger than the original hole.
Why do cracks keep coming back over doors and windows in Leander?

Central Texas clay soil swells when wet and shrinks when dry, and Leander homes move a little with it, especially in newer Larkspur, Bryson and Rancho Sienna builds and older homes on Mason Hills lots. Hairline cracks at door and window corners are usually cosmetic. Warning signs that are not just drywall: a crack wider than a credit card, a diagonal stair-step pattern, doors that suddenly stick, or a crack that reopens within weeks. If I see that pattern, I will tell you to get a foundation opinion first instead of selling you a patch that will not hold.
Can you match my existing wall texture?

Yes, and texture matching is the part most repairs get wrong. We identify the existing texture, orange peel, knockdown, skip trowel or smooth, test it, and match the pattern before finishing, so the patch is not visible once painted. Honest warning: popcorn ceilings from older homes are often impossible to match convincingly in one spot. The honest fix there is usually to scrape and refinish the whole ceiling, and we will say so up front.
Do you repair water-damaged ceilings?

Yes. We cut out the damaged section back to solid material, replace it, texture to match, and paint wall to wall. A water-damaged ceiling section runs $600-$1,500. Warning: if the leak is still active, fixing the drywall first wastes your money. Fix the leak, let the cavity dry, then call us. If the material is soft, sagging or moldy, it gets replaced, not patched over.
How long does drywall repair take, and why not same day?

Most repairs take 2 to 4 days, and most of that time is drying, not labor. Each coat of compound needs to dry fully, usually overnight, before the next coat. Rushing it with heat cracks the finish. For small repairs in Leander we can usually schedule within the same week. Text photos to 512-663-8867 and we will tell you the real timeline for your wall.
Do you paint after the repair?

Yes. We prime and paint the repaired wall corner to corner. Spot-painting only the patch almost always flashes, meaning you see a dull or shiny rectangle in daylight even when the texture is perfect. If you have the original paint and the wall is under about five years old, a spot blend sometimes works, and we will test it honestly before charging you for a full wall.

Composite or wood?

Do I need HOA approval for a deck in Austin?

Can you repair a deck instead of replacing it?

faq: How much does tree removal cost in Austin TX?

Angi's Austin-area data puts tree removal at about $736 on average, with most homeowners paying between $256 and $1,962 — by height, roughly $100–$400 for a tree up to 30 feet, $350–$1,100 at 30–60 feet, and $650–$1,350 at 60–80 feet, with tall or hard-to-reach trees running higher. When is it safe to trim oak trees in Austin?

July through January. Oak wilt spreads through fresh wounds, and the Texas A&M Forest Service recommends avoiding pruning or wounding oaks from February through June, when the beetles that carry it are most active. Austin's live oaks grow in connected groves — through Hyde Park, Tarrytown and Bouldin Creek — so one infected tree can move through a whole street. Every cut on an oak should be painted immediately, in any season — we follow both rules on every oak we touch, which makes fall and winter the right time to book oak work.
Do I need a permit to remove a tree in Austin?

Sometimes. The City of Austin protects trees 19 inches or more in diameter — removing or heavily pruning a protected tree needs a city tree permit first, and heritage trees (24 inches or more, including live oaks and pecans) get extra review. Dead or hazardous trees can qualify for an expedited approval, but the paperwork still comes first. HOAs in places like Circle C Ranch, Mueller and Steiner Ranch often require their own approval too. If a tree looks big enough to be covered, we'll flag it before quoting so its status can be confirmed with the city first.
Do you haul away the wood and grind the stump?

Yes. Haul-off is included unless you'd like to keep the firewood — pecan is worth keeping if you smoke or grill. Stump grinding is quoted as a separate line so you can decide — grinding goes below grade so you can plant, sod or mow over the spot.
A tree is touching a power line. Can you remove it?

Call your electric provider first — inside Austin that's usually Austin Energy, with Oncor and Pedernales Electric serving parts of the outskirts. Lines must be made safe by the utility before anyone works near them. Once they've cleared it, we can take care of the tree and the cleanup.

All of Austin — Hyde Park, Clarksville, Tarrytown, Bouldin Creek, Allandale, Crestview, Mueller, Circle C Ranch, Cherry Creek and Steiner Ranch — plus Leander, Cedar Park, Round Rock and Georgetown. We also handle common-area trees and storm cleanup for HOAs and property managers.
